etymology: Hebrew yeduthun, perhaps “praising” or “giver of praise,” one of the three chief musicians whom David set over the song of the house of the LORD, also called Ethan.
biblical_def: Jeduthun was one of the three chief Levites whom David set over the ministry of holy song, standing with Asaph and Heman as a master of the temple music (1Ch 25:1). His sons prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD, and he himself is named in the great work of thanksgiving when the ark was brought up, where he and Heman were appointed with trumpets and cymbals and instruments of God (1Ch 16:41-42). His name is written over three of the psalms, the thirty-ninth, the sixty-second, and the seventy-seventh, which were committed to him and his sons to lead in the worship of the sanctuary. The dictionary honours that Jeduthun was no mere musician for delight, but a man set apart to prophesy with the harp, that the praises of God might be sung in their appointed order. The song of the temple was not invented by men nor offered as it pleased them, but ordained of God through David His servant and the prophets. There is grace here for the singing church, for the LORD ordained that He should be praised in psalms upon the harp, and that His people should give thanks in the great congregation. Jeduthun stands as a witness that holy song is a ministry of the LORD’s own appointing, and that to lead the praises of God’s house is a prophetic and honourable calling, kept for ever in the record of His worship.

etymology: Hebrew shubael, “captive of God” or “return ye to God,” a son of Heman the king’s seer among the temple singers, to be distinguished from Shebuel son of Gershom the treasurer.
biblical_def: Shubael was a son of Heman, the king’s seer, numbered among the singers set apart for the song of the house of the LORD (1Ch 25:4). When the lots were cast for the four and twenty courses, the thirteenth fell to Shubael, to him, his sons, and his brethren, twelve in number (1Ch 25:20). He must be carefully distinguished from another of the same name, Shebuel the son of Gershom the son of Moses, who was ruler over the treasures of the house of the LORD; for the Chronicler spells both names alike in the Hebrew, yet the one was a keeper of the storehouse and the other a singer of praise. This Shubael of Heman’s house bore an office of song, lifting up the voice and the harp in the courts of God. The dictionary honours that the Spirit of God preserved each man in his own place, the treasurer and the singer, that the reader confound them not. There is grace here for the singing church, that the LORD assigns to every Levite his ministry and would have His worship offered by the appointed hands. Shubael the singer stands as a witness that the praise of God’s house is committed to chosen men, set in their courses by lot, and that the LORD who orders His sanctuary keeps the name of each singer distinct and sure in the record of His worship.

etymology: Hebrew yachaziel, “God sees” or “beheld of God,” a Levite of the sons of Asaph upon whom the Spirit of the LORD came to declare victory before Jehoshaphat.
biblical_def: Jahaziel was a Levite of the sons of Asaph, the son of Zechariah and of the singing line that ministered before the LORD, upon whom the Spirit of the LORD came in the midst of the congregation when Jehoshaphat and Judah cried unto God against a great host (2Ch 20:14). He lifted up his voice and said, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s; and on the morrow, when Judah went forth with singers praising the beauty of holiness, the LORD set ambushments and their enemies were overthrown (2Ch 20:15-17). A man of this name is also reckoned among the priests who sounded with trumpets before the ark of God in the day David brought it up (1Ch 16:6). The dictionary honours that the same line which led Israel’s praise was used of the LORD to speak His word of comfort and to herald His salvation. There is grace here for the singing church, that holy song and the word of the LORD go together, and that the people who praise the beauty of holiness are the people whom God defends. Jahaziel stands as a witness that the LORD who fills His house with song is the LORD of hosts who fights for His people, and that the battle is His; for they that trust Him and praise Him shall see His salvation, and the voice of thanksgiving shall outlast the noise of the enemy.
